To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pathogenic antibody for passive Heymann nephritigenesis in rats directs insertion of the C5b9 MAC into glomerular visceral (parietal) epithelial cell (GEC) plasma membranes with consequant cytotoxicity, including sublytic injury.

the pathogenic antibody in passive Heymann's nephritis (PH) directs insertion of complement C5b- 9 into the plasma membrane of glomerular visceral (parietal) epithelial cells with consequent cytolytic and sublytic injury.
the pathogenic antibody in PHN directs insertion of the C5b9 MAC into the plasma membrane of GEC, resulting in complement-dependent cytotoxic injury.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidation of the mechanisms whereby nephritogenic autoantibodies injure the glomerular epithelium in the rat model of passive Heymann nephritis.
the role of glomerular visceral cell (GVC) injury in the pathogenesis of immune complex glomerulonephritis.
the pathogenesis of membranous glomerulonephritis (MGN) in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pathogenic antibody in passive Heymann's nephritis produces complement-dependent cytolytic as well as non-cytolytic cytotoxicity in glomerular epithelia.
anti-Fx1a produces cytotoxicity of rat GEC in the presence of complement.
the antibody of PHN directs the insertion of the MAC in GEC plasma membranes, resulting in sublytic and lytic cytotoxic injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pathogenic antibody in this model is capable of inducing a variety of responses in GEC, including sublytic injury, blebbing, and cell death.
antibody-sensitized G cells are lysed in vitro by the MAC, and this process is associated with morphological changes that resemble those of the G cell in vivo in PHN.
sublytic cytotoxicity may be a mechanism for glomerular injury in PHN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
complement activation by nephritogenic antibody in vivo is likely to result in sublytic as opposed to lytic injury of glomerular visceral (epithelial) cells.
we found that complement-dependent cytotoxic effects on glomerular epithelium in PHN are mediated by the C8 component of the complement cascade.

the pathogenic antibody (gamma 1 anti-Fx1) of passive Heymann nephritigsis (PHN) is capable of directing the insertion of the C5b9 complement membrane attack complex (C5b9 MAC) into glomerular epithelium (GEC) plasma membranes with consequetnt cytotoxicity.
